title: Samsung Galaxy S25 vs. Galaxy S25+: Which One Should You Choose?
text:
Samsung Galaxy S25⁤ vs. Galaxy S25+: A Deep Dive ⁢into the Differences So,⁣ you have ⁢your heart set on a​ shiny ⁣new Samsung⁤ Galaxy S25 device? There’s definitely plenty to love about the Korean giant’s new flagship lineup. ⁣To be perfectly frank, it is a bit too similar to last year’s S24 ⁢family, at least ⁢for⁢ our taste, but that’s a whole other discussion. Today, ​we are looking at the choice between ​the ‌vanilla Galaxy S25 and the Galaxy S25+.
For many, this will ‌be an obvious choice that‌ simply comes down to ⁣size and/or price since the two devices practically ⁤share the⁣ same hardware. Still,there are a few subtle ‍differences here and ​there that might be worth pointing out.
For starters, you can compare the complete specs sheets or directly continue with our editor’s assessment⁤ in the following text.
Size Comparison let’s be frank: for most prospective buyers, size will be the big determining factor ⁣between the two devices. The vanilla S25 is a compact ⁣device with a‌ 6.2-inch display and 146.9 x 70.5 x 7.2 mm body, ⁤tipping the scale at just ‌162 grams.
In contrast, you get⁢ a pretty sizeable 6.7-inch ‌display with the Galaxy S25+.it measures 158.4 x 75.8 x⁤ 7.3 mm and weighs 190 grams,which is also ‌quite reasonable for its size.
For better or worse,unlike Apple,Samsung doesn’t ⁢offer ‍a compact “Ultra”,so ⁢to speak.If a⁤ small size ⁤is what you⁢ are after, ​then you have to make some⁤ hardware compromises.
One thing you‌ won’t have to realistically sacrifice, though, is build quality and materials. sure, the Ultra ‍still has somewhat of a leg up on⁢ the other two S25 models, but the S25 and S25+ are identical in this department ‌and deliver ⁢big. Both phones employ a premium “glass sandwich” construction with ‌gorilla⁣ Glass Victus 2 on both sides and ​an Armor aluminum 2 frame.
both phones also have ⁤the‌ same IP68 ingress protection rating, ⁣which⁢ should allow them to survive for up​ to 30 minutes in up ⁣to 1.5 meters ‌of fresh water.
Display⁣ Comparison Last year’s S24 generation marked ⁣a rather major display upgrade.​ Both ​models received LTPO tech ⁣for more dynamic⁢ refresh rate adjustment and better power efficiency. And the S24+ got its QHD resolution⁢ back, which was absent ​for a few generations.
This year,⁤ however, the panels for​ the S25 generation seem unchanged from last year on both the S25 and‍ S25+. We can’t exactly complain⁢ about thes particular panels ‍since they still hold up very well in the modern smartphone landscape. As mentioned, both are LTPO-based and offer a dynamic 120Hz refresh rate. Also, plenty of brightness and HDR10+ certification.
To be ​perfectly honest, it is a bummer that Samsung is still‍ sticking to 8-bit color depth displays on both models while most of its competitors have already advanced ‍to 10-bit and ‍even 12-bit color.
the display department ⁤is where we find one of the ​major differences between the S25 and S25+ – size. That one is obvious.‌ But beyond screen real estate, there is also ‌the more subtle difference in resolution. The ⁣S25+ comes​ with a QHD+ display, compared⁣ to the S25’s FHD+. This also translates to a difference in sharpness, with ​the ‍S25 peaking at around 416 ppi, compared to 513⁣ ppi‍ on the Plus model.‍ To ⁣be perfectly frank, however, the real-world difference is hard to spot unless you really pixel-peep, even in person, side by side.
Battery Life A bigger phone naturally means a bigger battery. The vanilla galaxy S25 comes with a 4,000 mAh battery,which is more than ​sufficient for a day’s use.‍ On the other hand, the⁢ S25+ boasts⁢ a ‍larger 4,800 mAh battery, providing even more juice for those who need it.

Both devices support fast charging,ensuring⁢ that you can quickly top ⁣up your battery when⁣ needed. Additionally, the S25 and S25+ both support wireless charging, making it convenient to‌ charge your ‍device without any cables.
Conclusion choosing between the Samsung Galaxy S25 and the Galaxy S25+ ultimately comes down to your personal preferences. If you prefer a⁤ more compact device, the vanilla S25 is the way to go. However, if you want a larger display and a bigger battery, the S25+ is the ⁢better choice.

Galaxy S25 & S25+ Specifications and Comparison The Galaxy⁢ S25 and S25+ smartphones from Samsung feature advanced AI capabilities, enhanced camera technology, and superior ‍display innovations. Both devices come with 12GB of RAM, but differ in storage options: the S25 starts at 128GB, while the S25+ begins at 256GB, with neither offering expandable storage.
One notable feature exclusive to the S25+ is Ultra Wideband (UWB)⁣ support, which is absent in the vanilla S25. in terms of software, both phones deliver the same One UI⁢ experience⁤ and a comprehensive feature​ set, including various Galaxy AI features. Additionally, both devices are promised⁤ seven major OS updates, ensuring long-term software support.
Benchmark Performance Powered by the top-tier Snapdragon 8 Elite chipset, both the ‌S25 and S25+ offer remarkable burst performance. The performance differences between the two are minimal, ⁤with any variations being due to run-to-run deviations. The S25+​ has a ⁣slight edge in sustained performance due to its larger size, which aids in better thermal management.
Camera Comparison The camera hardware on the Galaxy S25 and S25+‍ is⁤ identical, borrowing from the S24 and S24+ ⁣models.The primary difference lies in the new Image Signal Processor (ISP) that comes with ‍the Snapdragon 8‌ Elite chipset.
